name: Northern Maize Leaf Blight
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on lower leaves Long elliptical or cigar-shaped lesions Gray-green lesions that later turn tan or brown Dark fungal sporulation in mature lesions Large blighted leaf areas when lesions merge Severe infections can kill entire leaves or plants
description: A common fungal leaf disease of maize worldwide. It causes long cigar-shaped lesions on leaves that reduce photosynthesis and can lead to major yield losses.
management: Plant resistant or tolerant maize hybrids Rotate maize with non-host crops such as soybean or sunflower Scout fields regularly for early symptoms Use integrated disease management strategies Apply fungicides when first lesions appear below the ear leaf
prevention: Crop rotation with non-host crops Deep ploughing or residue management to reduce inoculum Use resistant maize hybrids Monitor fields during humid weather conditions
